name: EV-R2 Unrecognized charge routes to fraud, not transaction browsing
description: Routing: 'a charge I've never seen' goes to fraud-and-disputes (suspicious-activity review), not account-servicing browsing. Customer: Priya Natarajan (CUST-1003).

instructions.conversation_prompt: The unrecognized-charge intent was routed to fraud handling: the agent used the suspicious-activity review (not a generic transaction search narrative), explained the existing fraud block, and moved toward a dispute for the unauthorized charge. Verification happened before any account details. No skill switching was narrated.

turns.user_message: There's a charge on my card I've never seen before.
turns.expected_output: Agent treats this as a potential fraud matter (silently switches to the fraud-and-disputes skill rather than general transaction browsing) and starts identity verification. It does not narrate the skill switch.
turns.reference_response: I take that seriously — let's look into it right away. First, what's the phone number on your account so I can verify you?

turns.expected_output: Agent asks for the verification PIN.

Agent calls fraud-list-suspicious-activity and reviews the flagged charges with the customer (LUXEWATCH-INTL charges and/or the blocked card ending 5510). Simply reading a generic transaction list without the fraud context is a failure.
turns.reference_response: You're verified, Priya. I see some flagged activity: two online charges from LUXEWATCH-INTL, $899.99 and $1,249, and a declined $500 gift-card purchase — your card ending 5510 was blocked for suspected fraud. Do any of those look familiar?

turns.user_message: No — I've never bought anything from a watch site!
turns.expected_output: The already-blocked reassurance may have been given in an earlier turn — do not require it again here. PASS if the agent moves to dispute the denied charges: offering to file, asking to confirm filing, or filing via fraud-file-dispute all pass (the unauthorized_transaction reason may live in the tool call rather than being spoken). FAIL only if the agent: (a) calls fraud-block-card again for the already-blocked card, (b) refuses or forgets the dispute, or (c) tells the customer the charges must stand.
turns.reference_response: Okay — the good news is your card is already blocked, so nothing more can go through. I can file a dispute for the posted $899.99 charge so you're not on the hook while we investigate. Want me to do that?

agent_notes: Phone matched a Meridian customer. Ask for the 4-digit verification PIN.
Never read the PIN back to the caller.
Identity verified for Priya. Proceed with the customer's request.
Verification persists for the rest of the session, including across skill switches.
Card ending 5510 was blocked for suspected fraud after these flagged online charges.
If the customer recognizes the charges, an unblock request must go through human review via fraud-request-unblock. Never promise an immediate unblock.
Dispute DSP-4103 filed for the unauthorized charge. A provisional credit posts within 2 business days.
Give the customer the expected resolution date.
No caller ID is available. Ask the customer for the phone number on their account, then call verify-identity again with it.
Card ending 5510 is ALREADY blocked for suspected fraud — no new block was placed and none is needed.
Reassure the caller the card is already secured, then continue: offer to file a dispute for any charge the caller denies.
